title: Officer cleared in fatal shooting; Action likely saved wife of Windsor man, says SIU
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has concluded that a Toronto police officer did not commit a criminal offence when he shot and killed a Windsor man earlier this year.
The man was stabbing his wife and the shooting may have saved her life, SIU director James Cornish concluded.
On March 28, Toronto police were called to an apartment on Keele Street where Cristian Iordache, 37, his wife Adriana and their children were visiting with Adriana's brother George Coltea.
Police were called to the apartment by neighbours who were reporting a domestic disturbance at 8:46 a.m.
The SIU investigation determined that Iordache had started to hit his wife while chasing her around the apartment.
Adriana ran into a common hallway with Iordache in pursuit, and she then re-entered the apartment.
Iordache then grabbed a meat cleaver and began attacking her with it.

The first police officer arrived at 8:49 a.m. and was directed into the apartment by neighbours, one of whom told the officer he believed Iordache was going to kill his wife and that he may be armed with a knife.
The officer saw fresh blood on the walls and a door frame and heard a woman crying, the SIU said.
The officer entered the apartment and saw Iordache holding a large two-pronged barbecue fork and Adriana bleeding from her chest.
The officer pulled his gun and yelled "drop the knife" at Iordache, who ignored the officer and grabbed his wife and began stabbing her in the neck.
The officer fired a single gunshot, striking Iordache in the chest. Iordache let go of his wife and fell to the floor and appeared to have no vital signs.
Iordache was rushed to Sunnybrook Hospital but was pronounced dead at 9:56 a.m.
Adriana was taken to Humber River Regional Hospital where she was treated for a deep cut to her hand, puncture wounds to her neck and bruising and swelling.

"I believe that the subject officer had an honestly held belief that if he did not shoot, Mr. Iordache would have stabbed his wife and caused her grievous bodily harm or worse," said Cornish in a news release.
"Unfortunately, Mr. Iordache died as a result. Fortunately, Mrs. Iordache was saved from further injury."

The investigation involved 17 police and civilian witnesses, and forensic identification technicians examined the officer's firearm and uniform, a meat cleaver, barbecue fork and bullet cartridge case.
An aunt of Adriana Iordache declined comment when contacted by The Star.
The couple had recently purchased a home in the Devonshire Heights subdivision.
Adriana Iordache's parents live in Romania.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians which result in sexual assault,
